findings.title: v1 failure details reach the PR comment as live Markdown/HTML (mentions, remote images, links)
findings.where: .github/scripts/prepare_report.py (v1 branch: summary = full `arci report` Markdown); src/arci/report.py:469 failure-cluster row via _cell, which escapes only | and newline
findings.claim: For v1 stores the comment body is the whole v1 Markdown report, including the 'Example failure detail' column. That column holds trial.failure_detail: agent exception text (CRASH uses `Name: message`) and contract violation details, which can echo model output. It is not neutralised, so @user and @org/team mentions notify people, ![..](https://..) and fetch remote content through camo, and phishing links render in a comment posted by github-actions[bot]. Suite summaries are safe because task and condition ids are restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._-].
findings.evidence: Scratch test test_v1_failure_detail_markdown_injection_reaches_comment (scratchpad/p4review/test_p4_review.py) builds a v1 store from tests.unit.html_report v1_evidence() with candidate failure_detail "ValueError: model said @octocat cc @github/security ![p](https://evil.test/pixel.png) [approve](https://evil.test/phish)", then runs prepare() and post_comment() against a fake API. The posted body contains that string verbatim: `| `fff…` | 12 | ValueError: model said @octocat cc @github/security ![p](https://evil.test/pixel.png) [approve](https://evil.test/phish) |`.
findings.fix: Build the v1 comment from structured fields, as the suite branch does (verdict, per-arm n/successes, per-condition verdicts, hard violations, fault flags), and leave free-text failure details to the HTML artifact. If any free text must stay, neutralise it for GitHub Markdown: escape @ (for example @​), [ ] ( ) ! < > and backticks, or put it in a fenced code block with backticks stripped. Add a test asserting that no @, ![,

findings.title: A skipped comment leaves the previous run's verdict on the PR as if it were current
findings.where: .github/scripts/pr_comment.py post_comment early returns (artifact URL check, summary read in the except path, len(body) > 65000); action.yml steps report/artifact/comment
findings.claim: Whenever the comment step skips, it returns without touching the existing sticky comment. The comment also carries no commit SHA or run id, so readers cannot see that it is stale. Two concrete cases: (1) `arci run` fails before writing a store (gate ERROR, exit 3), prepare_report prints 'ARCI report unavailable', report_dir is unset, upload is skipped, and the comment step returns 'skipped: HTML artifact unavailable'; (2) the body exceeds 65,000 characters. In both cases a PASS comment from an earlier push stays on the PR while the current run is ERROR or BLOCK.
findings.evidence: gate_sim.sh, which replays action.yml's gate run block plus prepare_report.py, on a broken descriptor gives `gate exit=3`, `verdict=ERROR`, 'ARCI report unavailable; gate result unchanged.' and no report_dir in GITHUB_OUTPUT. Scratch test test_stale_comment_left_when_skipped[artifact|summary-missing|too-big] creates a 'VERDICT: PASS' comment, writes a BLOCK summary, then reproduces each skip: 'ARCI comment skipped: HTML artifact unavailable.' / 'API or report unavailable' / 'summary exceeds comment size limit.' All three pass with the stored comment still containing 'VERDICT: PASS'.
findings.fix: Pass steps.gate.outputs.verdict and github.sha / run URL into the comment step. When a marker comment exists and the full summary cannot be posted, PATCH it to a minimal body ('ARCI verdict for <sha>: ERROR; report unavailable, see run <url>') instead of skipping. Include the head SHA in every body. If the summary is too large, truncate the fault table rather than skipping.

findings.title: Suite comment omits the verdict reason and the hard-violation count; a hard-violation BLOCK reads as an unexplained BLOCK with candidate 20/20
findings.where: .github/scripts/prepare_report.py suite branch (summary lines: VERDICT, per-arm counts, Pairs line, guarantee/assumption text, fault table)
findings.claim: The suite summary keeps only the VERDICT line from `arci report` and drops 'Reasons:' and the hard-violations column. docs/STATISTICS_SUITE.md line 271 says a candidate hard-violation BLOCK is outside the false-BLOCK bound and 'Reports must show the reason.' The word 'hard' appears nowhere except the generic assumptions sentence.
findings.fix: Add the 'Reasons:' line (decision.reasons) and the candidate hard-violation count from the last history row to the suite summary. Extend test_prepare_report with a hard-violation store.

findings.title: With pr-comment left at its default, existing users still get stderr capture, an HTML report step and an artifact upload on every run
findings.where: action.yml: gate step `2> >(tee arci-run.stderr >&2)`; 'Prepare offline HTML report' (if: always() && steps.gate.outcome != 'skipped'); 'Upload HTML report' (if: always() && steps.report.outputs.report_dir != '')
findings.claim: Only the comment step checks inputs.pr-comment. Every current user of the Action, including the repository's own action-fixture CI job, now gets: a new arci-run.stderr file in the workspace; an extra `arci report` pass; and a new arci-report-XXXX artifact on every run, which uses artifact storage and retention. On runners where upload-artifact v7 is unsupported (GHES, older self-hosted runners) they also get a failed (continue-on-error) step annotation. The 'default off, no change' expectation does not hold.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD -- action.yml` shows the gate run line changed and two new unconditional steps. Neither the report nor the artifact step mentions inputs.pr-comment; test_action_keeps_gate_exit_and_comment_opt_in asserts the opt-in only for steps[-1]. Exit codes are preserved: a local replay of the ci.yml summary check gives gate exit=1, summary identical and stderr not leaked, and the existing action tests pass.
findings.fix: Gate the prepare and upload steps on the opt-in (`inputs.pr-comment == 'true'`), or add a separate `html-report` input that defaults to false. Otherwise record the always-on artifact as a deliberate, documented behaviour change in the release notes and README Action section.

findings.title: Every Action invocation on a PR shares one marker, so several manifests or workflows overwrite each other's verdict
findings.where: .github/scripts/pr_comment.py MARKER = "<!-- arci-reliability-report -->" and the github-actions[bot] match
findings.claim: The marker carries no identity for the experiment, manifest or job. A workflow that runs the Action on two manifests (a matrix, two steps or two workflows) edits one comment, and the last writer wins. A BLOCK from one suite disappears from the PR when another suite PASSes.
findings.evidence: Scratch test test_two_action_invocations_share_one_comment posts 'VERDICT: BLOCK … suite one' and then 'VERDICT: PASS … suite two' with the same repository and PR. Exactly one comment remains, and it no longer contains BLOCK.
findings.fix: Derive the marker from a stable key, for example `<!-- arci-reliability-report:<sha256 of manifest path or experiment suite_id> -->` (passed via env from inputs.manifest), and match on that full marker.

findings.title: Racing runs create duplicate sticky comments, and the duplicates are never reconciled
findings.claim: Without workflow concurrency, two runs that both list before either posts each create a comment. The input description only recommends concurrency. After that, every later run PATCHes only the lowest id, so the second comment keeps an old verdict forever.
findings.evidence: Scratch test test_race_two_runs_both_create gives both calls a stale (empty) listing, which yields 2 comments. A third normal call returns 'ARCI comment updated.' and still leaves 2 comments, one of them stale.
findings.fix: After a POST, re-list and delete or PATCH any other marker comments, or PATCH every found id (and optionally delete all but the oldest), so duplicates converge.

findings.title: Large suites exceed the size cap and get no comment at all, with no truncation
findings.where: .github/scripts/pr_comment.py `if len(body) > 65000: return skipped`; prepare_report.py fault table has one row per condition x fault x arm
findings.claim: The fault-accounting table grows with conditions x faults x 2. Above 65,000 characters the script silently skips instead of truncating, and any existing comment is left stale (see the stale-comment finding).
findings.evidence: Scratch test test_large_suite_summary_size2 (1 task x 300 conditions with 54-character ids, one fault each) produces a 76,832-character summary.md, and post_comment returns 'ARCI comment skipped: summary exceeds comment size limit.' with 0 comments created.
findings.fix: Cap the fault table (for example, list only never-fired or unusual rows and summarise the rest) and append 'table truncated; see HTML report', keeping the body under 65,536 characters.

I could not refute this finding. In /Users/ajay/Developer/.arci-worktrees/wt-v2-integration/.github/scripts/pr_comment.py the marker is the constant MARKER = "<!-- arci-reliability-report -->". Lookup matches any github-actions[bot] comment whose body starts with MARKER + "\n", then PATCHes min(found). I wrote my own scratch test at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p4review/marker/test_marker.py, with a fake API that keeps state. The test passed with pytest -p no:cacheprovider.

The brief (P4 lines 35-37) asks for "one sticky comment" found by a hidden marker. That is right for a single invocation. Neither the brief, the action input description nor the script docstring says that more than one manifest per PR is unsupported. corrected_claim: pr_comment.py uses a fixed marker that carries no identity for the manifest, suite or job. When the Action runs with pr-comment: true on more than one manifest for the same PR (a matrix, two steps or two workflows), every run PATCHes the same github-actions[bot] comment and the last writer wins. I reproduced it: posting BLOCK for suite one, then PASS for suite two, leaves one comment containing only the PASS. The failing check of the BLOCK job still shows on the PR, so the gate is not bypassed, but the sticky summary is misleading. Fix: put a stable key in the marker, for example a hash of inputs.manifest or the suite_id passed through env, and match on the full marker.

findings.title: Sticky comment is left stale, showing the previous verdict, when this run produces no report or artifact
findings.where: .github/scripts/pr_comment.py post_comment (early return 'HTML artifact unavailable' and the size-limit return); action.yml 'Update pull request comment' step
findings.claim: If arci run produces no store (for example an invalid manifest, i.e. exit 3 ERROR), or the HTML step or artifact upload fails, or the body exceeds 65000 characters, post_comment returns before listing or patching comments. The earlier sticky comment stays on the PR. It says, for example, 'VERDICT: PASS' and names no commit or run, so readers take a stale verdict for the current one while the job fails.
findings.evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p4review/comment_probe.py part A. findings.fix: When a token and PR context are present but no report or artifact exists, still find the marker comment and PATCH it with a short body: the gate's verdict output or 'report unavailable for <sha>'. Also put the head SHA and run id in every body so staleness can be seen.

findings.title: BLOCK meaning sentence is a generic disjunction and does not say the candidate is worse than the baseline
findings.claim: The sentence shown under the verdict is 'The suite mean dropped beyond the registered margin, or the candidate broke a hard invariant.' The decision's reasons already say which branch applies ('regression established' versus 'candidate hard violation'). 'The suite mean dropped' does not say it is the candidate-minus-baseline mean, so a reader can take it as the candidate's absolute success rate. The v1 report states it exactly: 'the candidate is worse than the baseline by more than the configured delta'.
findings.evidence:
study.html (study run, reason 'regression established', minus 26 / zero 70 / plus 0) renders `

The suite mean dropped beyond the registered margin, or the candidate broke a hard invariant.

`. The v1.html of the same build says 'BLOCK means the candidate is worse than the baseline by more than the configured delta, or it broke a hard invariant.'
findings.fix: Choose the sentence from decision.reasons. For a statistical BLOCK: 'On the suite mean, the candidate's success is lower than the baseline's by more than the registered margin (delta).' For a hard-violation BLOCK: 'The candidate broke a hard invariant; this BLOCK is not a statistical finding.'

reasoning:
I reproduced the behaviour; nothing under the worktree was changed. Scratch files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ajay--claude-spares-spare-8K9guD/39ca2335-7a5a-47d9-a374-69d92a47e1d0/scratchpad/p4review/skeptic_stale/.

(1) Gate ERROR before any store exists. `arci run bad.json`, given an invalid manifest, exits 3 ("ValidationError: 7 validation errors for Manifest"). arci-run.stderr has no "run store:" line. prepare_report.py prints "ARCI report unavailable; gate result unchanged." and writes nothing to GITHUB_OUTPUT. As a result, report_dir is empty, the upload step is skipped and artifact-url is empty.

(2) I fed post_comment a fake API that already holds a "VERDICT: PASS" marker comment, and tested three cases:
- ARCI_SUMMARY="/summary.md" with an empty ARCI_ARTIFACT_URL returns "ARCI comment skipped: HTML artifact unavailable."
- A valid artifact URL with a missing summary returns "skipped: API or report unavailable".
- A BLOCK summary over 66,000 characters returns "skipped: summary exceeds comment size limit."

In all three cases the API received zero calls and the stored comment still says PASS. The code confirms it: every one of these early returns happens before the GET/PATCH, so a skipped run never touches the existing sticky comment.

I narrowed two parts of the finding:
- It says the comment carries no run id. That is partly wrong: the body ends with the artifact link, whose path is /{repo}/actions/runs/<run_id>/artifacts/..., so the run id is there, though not in a form that tells a reader the comment is stale. The commit SHA really is missing.
- Severity. The job's check status is still correct: the gate step exits with 3 or 1, so the PR shows a red check. The PASS text was true for the commit it was written for. The brief requires create/update/fail-soft and says nothing about invalidating a stale comment. So this is a fix-before-release defect (a misleading stale verdict next to a failing check), not a wrong number or sentence produced by the code. Case (1) is realistic: any gate ERROR before a store is written triggers it. The oversized-body case is possible but unlikely for typical summaries.
corrected_claim: When the comment step skips, the existing sticky comment is left unchanged. This happens when the HTML artifact URL is missing (for example, `arci run` exits 3 on an invalid manifest, so prepare_report writes no report_dir and the upload is skipped), when the summary is missing, or when the body exceeds 65,000 characters. A PASS comment from an earlier push then stays on the PR while the current run is ERROR or BLOCK. The body includes no commit SHA; the run id appears only inside the artifact link. The failing check status still gates the PR correctly, so this is a misleading stale comment (major), not a wrong gate result.
